CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine follow-up with chronic medical conditions.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Eugene Walker is a 61-year-old male with significant cardiac history presenting for routine follow-up. The patient underwent aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on 1/22/2013. He reports increased fatigue, particularly after prolonged physical exertion. He continues to bike regularly 20-30 miles at a time, though states he is more tired and requires rest upon arriving home compared to prior years when he could complete 40-mile rides. He denies this is related to depression and reports overall good mood. The patient noted his wife and friends have observed pursed lip breathing when he walks but denies any associated wheezing. He is concerned about the longevity of his aortic valve replacement and requested evaluation with an echocardiogram. He also reports noticing a small nodule on his right testicle epididymis and wanted medical evaluation of this finding. He denies routine testicular self-exams and states he is not overly concerned about the nodule.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports fatigue and pursed lip breathing without wheezing. Denies shortness of breath with exertion despite fatigue. Wife reports patient snores but denies observed apnea. No other significant review of systems findings documented.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Aortic valve replacement with ascending aortic aneurysm repair (1/22/2013).

MEDICATIONS
Vitamin D3 50,000 units on Sundays and 2,000 units on other days of the week. Clindamycin prior to dental procedures.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a lecturer and is required to be at work by 7:00 AM. He exercises regularly, biking 20-30 miles and swimming twice weekly at 5:45 AM. He attempts morning workouts when possible. Patient sleeps 6-7 hours per night. Wife reports mild snoring. Patient does not routinely follow up at Hopkins due to stress and instead receives intermittent local follow-ups.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Patient appears well overall.
Respiratory: Pursed lip breathing noted with low exhalation phase. Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezing.
Genitalia: Right testicle with 2-3 millimeter palpable nodule, not consistent with epididymis or varicocele. Left testicle normal. No hernia palpable.
All other portions of physical examination normal.

RESULTS
Prior laboratory work from 4/10/2021:
- Alkaline phosphatase: 156 (elevated)
- Total cholesterol: 247
- HDL: 66
- LDL: 166
- Triglycerides: 74
- TSH: 2.68 (normal)
- CBC: unremarkable
- Vitamin D: 94 (high end of normal)

Last stress test: September 9, 2019.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. History of aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair: Patient doing well and currently asymptomatic. Will refer to cardiology with Dr. Vincent Sanchez. Echocardiogram and stress test ordered for further evaluation.

2. Elevated alkaline phosphatase (156): Most likely related to bone health. Will order repeat alkaline phosphatase and GGT testing today. Results to be sent via patient portal unless critically abnormal, in which case patient will be contacted.

3. Pursed lip breathing with exhalation abnormality: Noted on examination. Patient reports fatigue with exertion. Pulmonary function testing ordered for further evaluation.

4. Right testicular nodule (2-3 millimeters): Referral to urology placed for possible ultrasound evaluation.

5. Preventive health: MMR vaccine to be administered today. Shingles vaccine recommended, to be scheduled for next month at front desk. COVID-19 vaccination series completed (first dose 1/15/2021, second dose 2/5/2021).

Patient to return for wellness visit in one year, sooner if needed based on laboratory and study results. Patient instructed to call with any questions or concerns.
